name: GML
title: GML (2026.0)

presenceList.meta: R1, Ec4, Ec5, Ec6, Ec8, D1, D3, S2

type.text: **Variables are dynamically typed**: A name takes any value, and `typeof` reads the type at run time
**A script is a value**: `script_execute` and a method variable dispatch at run time
**There are no sum types**: A state is an integer and a `switch`
**There are no namespaces**: Every script, object, and global lives in one project scope
**There are no generics**: A data structure holds any value
**An unset variable is `undefined`**: The type does not carry the check

construction.text: **An instance's Create event is its constructor**: The engine calls it once
**Instance and global variables are shared by default**: A `global.` variable is reachable from every object
**A variable is mutable by default**: A struct is the only value with a copy semantic

memory.text: **The runtime frees an instance**: `instance_destroy` and the collector release memory
**There is no scope-exit release**: A data structure or a surface is freed by a call
**Aliasing is unrestricted**: Two references can hold one struct, and nothing marks the owner

error.text: **There is no exception path**: A failed call writes a message and continues, and `show_error` aborts

concurrency.text: **The game loop is the only thread**: Everything runs on one thread and one frame

platform.text: **A program runs inside the GameMaker runtime**: The engine provides the loop, the renderer, and the objects
**The same project exports to many targets**: Windows, macOS, Linux, HTML5, mobile, and consoles

performance.text: **The default target is a bytecode VM**: The YoYo Compiler can emit C++ for a native build
**A native build is available**: The YYC path trades a long build for native speed

ecosystem.text: **The engine is proprietary**: GameMaker is licensed, and the source is closed
**The IDE is the toolchain**: The editor, the debugger, and the build are one application
**The engine is the ecosystem**: A library outside the asset marketplace is rare
**The asset marketplace is the package source**: An extension is installed from the IDE
**An extension binds to the toolchain**: GameMaker documents extension packages built against the IDE and runner release [@gmExtensions]
**Stored projects cross on a documented conversion**: the IDE detects a pre-2.3.0 project on import, converts it, and generates a compatibility report to check [@gmProjectFormat]

evolution.text: **The engine ships on a monthly and an LTS channel**: A project can pin a stable line
**The language follows the engine**: A runtime rewrite can change an idiom

domain.text: **The domain is 2D games**: The engine's objects, sprites, and rooms are the model
**The event model sets the architecture**: A game is a set of objects and event handlers

learning.text: **A beginner can ship a game quickly**: Drag-and-drop actions and a small language

syntax.text: **Two dialects share the editor**: GML Visual and GML code state the same action
**The syntax is C-like**: Braces, semicolons, and functions

testing.text: **The debugger steps through an instance**: Watches and breakpoints are in the IDE

security.text: **There is no eval**: The engine does not run a string as code

reproducibility.text: **The build embeds the project and the runtime**: The artifact is not byte-identical across machines
**The engine version is the dependency**: A project records the runtime version

supplychain.text: **An extension is installed without a signature check**

observability.text: **There is no tracing standard**: `show_debug_message` writes to the console

feedback.text: **The IDE reports a compile error in place**

governance.text: **One vendor governs the engine and the language**

tradeoffs: **The engine buys the loop and the renderer**: A game starts from objects and events, not from a window
**The project scope is flat**: A global is reachable from every object, and the name is the contract
**The runtime is the platform**: An extension is a DLL or a marketplace asset, and it is not portable
**The language follows the engine's cadence**: A project pins an LTS line, and an update is a decision
verdict: GML is a game-engine language: the Create event and the runtime's object model make a small game cheap, and the exporter reaches many platforms, but the dynamic types, the flat project scope, the global state, the single game-loop thread, and the vendor runtime keep the coupling high. Main strength: a tight loop from an idea to a playable build. Main weakness: the program runs only inside one engine, and nothing in the type system checks it.

energy.text: No independent energy or time benchmark for the language is recorded.

ai-readiness.text: Sparse public training data: models write it less reliably than a mainstream language [@joel2025lowresource].

safety.text: No certified or standards-qualified path for safety-critical systems.

delivery.note: The IDE compiles GML inside the build of the whole game
GameMaker documents extension packages that link external SDK code, built against the IDE and runner release

data_formats.note: GameMaker documents the project formats per version and the reading direction the IDE takes: a project stored in a format older than 2.3.0 is detected on import, converted, and reported, and the format changed with that update
